topic.title: variant
topic.p: variant<A, B, ...> stores one declared option and its value. Option order is part of the type. There are no implicit conversions to or from variants.

Supported operators are:
=: assign the same ordered variant type.
cast: construct a variant, extract a declared option, or convert to another variant with at least one shared option.
of: construct a variant or convert to another variant containing every source option.
as: extract a pointer or nullable option, returning null when another option is active.
variant in VALUE: extract the active payload as object.
==, !=, <, >, <= and >=: compare active payloads, including variants of different types and nonvariant values.
is null and is not null: test the active payload when the variant has a null-bearing option.
in and not in: test membership in a typed enumerable, list or array whose element type is the exact same variant. Dictionaries are unsupported.
? : and ??: select between values of the same variant type.

Arithmetic, logical operations and member access require extracting an option first. cast object VALUE only extracts a declared object option; it does not box a complete variant. Use variant in VALUE to get any active payload as object.

topic.title: struct
topic.p: A struct is not allowed to have its nullable type as a direct or indirect field.
